take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only when the pieces need different access, a different dialect or a different stance, and be able to say which of the three it is.
The trouble is at the handoffs between agents. Two sources can disagree and one quietly wins, and nobody checks whether the final briefing is true.
Before an agent touches anything sensitive, ask what the worst thing it could do with that access is, and make risky steps 'propose' with a human approving.

monday.move: Ask my HR business partner and the DPO what they'd need to see before an agent may read employee data, then draft a weekly people-metrics summary agent that only proposes.
monday.who: Me, one HR partner, and the DPO
monday.when: Monday for the questions, later in the week for the draft
monday.stop_condition: Stop if the works council or DPO says employee data can't go in this tool.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked them yet.

misconception.why: The module never said what this means for roles, hiring or headcount, so I still think headcount goes first. 'Start with don't' and the access point made me more careful about how, but they did not change who I think goes.

one_line: Good rule of thumb that you shouldn't split agents without a reason, but it's all about the agents and almost nothing about the people they affect.
